chapterNote: A Song of Ascents about geography as theology. The pilgrim coming up to Jerusalem sees the city sitting in a bowl of hills, and he says: that is what trusting the LORD is like. Those who trust are like Mount Zion — it does not move; it stays forever — and as the mountains stand around Jerusalem, so the LORD stands around His people, from now on and forever. The middle verse is the realist's clause: the scepter of wickedness will not stay resting on the land allotted to the righteous, because if it did, the righteous themselves might reach out their hands to do wrong — God limits the trial to what faith can bear (Paul's promise in 1 Corinthians 10:13 has this psalm's shape). Then the prayer sorts two roads: do good, LORD, to the good and the upright in heart; but those who turn off onto their crooked byways, the LORD will march them off with the workers of iniquity. And the benediction that closes two of the Ascents, this one and Psalm 128: peace be upon Israel.

1.text: A song of ascents. Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but stays forever.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth]. They that trust [batach] in the LORD [YHWH] shall be as mount [har] Zion [Tsiyyon], which cannot be removed [mot — toppled], but abides [yashab — remains seated] for ever [olam].
1.notes: ha-botechim ba-YHWH ke-har-Tsiyyon (H982, H3068, H2022, H6726): the trusters like Mount Zion — lo-yimmot le-olam yeshev (H4131, H5769, H3427): it does not totter; it SITS forever, yashab, sit, dwell — the same le-olam yeshev that Psalm 9:7 says of the LORD enthroned. Trust makes a person as stationary as the mountain the temple sits on.

2.text: As the mountains stand all around Jerusalem, so the LORD stands all around His people, from now on and forever.
2.amp: As the mountains [har] are round about [sabib] Jerusalem [Yerushalaim], so the LORD [YHWH] is round about His people [am] from henceforth even for [ad] ever [olam].
2.notes: Yerushalaim harim sabib lah (H3389, H2022, H5439): Jerusalem is not on the highest hill — Olivet and Scopus overlook it — it sits in a ring of them, which is the picture: va-YHWH sabib le-ammo (H3068, H5971): the LORD around His people the way the hills are around the city — me-attah ve-ad-olam (H5704, H5769): from now on and forever. The pilgrim looks up at the skyline and sees a doctrine.

3.text: For the scepter of wickedness will not stay resting on the land allotted to the righteous — lest the righteous stretch out their hands to do wrong.
3.amp: For the rod [shebet — scepter] of the wicked ['wickedness', resha, the KJV margin] shall not rest [nuach] upon the lot [goral — allotment] of the righteous [tsaddiq]; lest [maan] the righteous put forth [shalach] their hands [yad] unto iniquity [avlah].
3.notes: ki lo yanuach shebet ha-resha al goral ha-tsaddiqim (H5117, H7626, H7562, H1486, H6662): the scepter of WICKEDNESS — the margin's abstract — will not come to REST on the righteous' allotted land: it may fall there, but it will not stay — le-maan lo-yishlechu ha-tsaddiqim be-avlatah yedehem (H4616, H7971, H6662, H5766, H3027): lest the righteous reach out and do wrong themselves. God caps the oppression at what faith can bear before it corrupts (cf. 1 Corinthians 10:13).

4.text: Do good, O LORD, to the good, and to those whose hearts are upright.
4.amp: Do good [tob — deal well], O LORD [YHWH], unto those that be good [tob], and to them that are upright [yashar] in their hearts [libbah].
4.notes: hetibah YHWH la-tobim (H2895, H3068, H2896): do good to the good — the verb and the adjective from one root, the prayer asking God's goodness to answer the goodness He has worked in them — ve-li-sharim be-libbotam (H3477, H3826): and to the straight in their hearts. Not the outwardly correct: the heart-straight.

5.text: But those who turn aside onto their crooked byways, the LORD will lead them away with the workers of iniquity. Peace be upon Israel!
5.amp: As for such as turn aside [natah — bend away] unto their crooked ways [aqalqal — winding, twisted paths], the LORD [YHWH] shall lead them forth [yalak] with the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven]: but peace [shalom] shall be upon Israel [Yisrael].
5.notes: ve-ha-mattim aqalqallotam (H5186, H6128): those BENDING onto their winding ways — aqalqal is a tortuous, twisting track, Judges 5:6's byways — yolikhem YHWH et-poale ha-aven (H3212, H3068, H6466, H205): the LORD will march them off with the evildoers. shalom al-Yisrael (H7965, H3478): peace upon Israel — the benediction that also ends Psalm 128:6, and that Paul adapts for the Israel of God (cf. Galatians 6:16).
